name: fossel-git-drift-v1
description: Git-aware drift fixtures (#31). Each memory references one file and declares the drift state that file should be in at read time: 'unchanged' (committed, untouched), 'committed-change' (content changed in a later commit), 'working-tree-dirty' (edited but not committed), or 'deleted' (removed and committed). The harness builds a scratch git repo deterministically from `files`, records file refs for every memory, then applies each memory's drift state, so findStaleFileRefs can be scored without any dependency on live repo state. Queries point at the memories whose files drifted, which is the signal #30 (drift-aware ranking) will use. The 'contested' queries add lexical interference: two memories match a shared query near-equally but differ in drift state, so a drift-aware ranking change has measurable headroom (the per-state queries are 1:1 with memories and already saturate FTS at 1.0).

memories.note: JWT verification lives in src/auth/jwt.ts and never trusts the client claim.
Role checks go through canAccess() in src/auth/rbac.ts, not the raw claim.
The Stripe client is constructed once in src/payments/stripe.ts from STRIPE_KEY.
Refunds are issued through refund() in src/payments/refund.ts, which wraps the Stripe API.
The database connection pool caps at 10 connections in src/db/pool.ts.
Pending migrations run at startup via migrate() in src/db/migrate.ts.
Redis is the session cache, wired up in src/cache/redis.ts from REDIS_URL.
All environment config is loaded once in src/config/env.ts.
Deploys go out through the release workflow documented in docs/deploy.md on a tag push.
The legacy SOAP client in src/legacy/soap.ts was removed in the 4.0 refactor.
The queue worker consumes the jobs stream. See src/queue/worker.ts.
The queue worker consumes the jobs stream with a bounded retry policy. See src/queue/retry.ts for the worker retry config.
HTTP rate limiting is enforced. See src/http/rate-limit.ts.
HTTP rate limiting is enforced with a fixed request window and per-client limit counters. See src/http/limits.ts for the rate limiting window and limit values.

queries.rationale: src/auth/jwt.ts changed in a later commit; the memory should read as drifted.
src/db/pool.ts was changed and committed after the memory was written.

queries.query: how is the Stripe client configured
queries.rationale: src/payments/stripe.ts has an uncommitted working-tree edit.
src/cache/redis.ts is dirty in the working tree.

queries.query: is the SOAP client still used
queries.rationale: src/legacy/soap.ts was deleted and committed; the file no longer resolves at HEAD.
src/auth/rbac.ts is untouched; the memory must NOT read as drifted.

queries.query: queue worker consumes jobs stream retry policy
queries.rationale: m-worker-fresh (unchanged, src/queue/retry.ts) wins pure FTS here: it repeats 'retry policy' and 'worker', so it carries more query terms. m-worker-drifted (committed-change, src/queue/worker.ts) is the intended answer but sits at rank 2 under FTS alone. Only a drift-aware ranking signal can lift it to rank 1, so MRR moves 0.5 -> 1.0 when #30 works and regresses if the drift hypothesis is wrong.

queries.query: HTTP rate limiting request window per-client limit
queries.rationale: Mirror of q-contested-worker for a working-tree-dirty file. m-rl-fresh (unchanged, src/http/limits.ts) carries more query terms ('request window', 'per-client limit') and wins pure FTS; m-rl-drifted (working-tree-dirty, src/http/rate-limit.ts) is the intended answer at rank 2. Guards against a drift signal that only rewards committed changes and ignores dirty working trees.
